newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT - Holidays, systems undermine trade.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT - Holidays, systems undermine trade.

text.p: A short trading week in Britain, a holiday on the Bombay Stock Exchange and price feed problems undermined trading in Indian global depositary receipts (GDRs).
"It has been very quiet. System problems and a general lack of interest has cut away this market," said a trader.
The U.S. Labor Day holiday next week also means that interest in New York in the market is limited, traders said.
"There are a few buyers looking at the premiums, but not much else," said a trader.
If India proceeds with plans to include GDRs in the level of stock allowed to be owned by foreigners, this could further undermine the market, traders said.
The Korea Composite Index fell 8.40 points to 753.35, a 34 month low.
"ADRs are the only free float in Korea, they are the only way foreigners can access this market," said an Asia trader.
Korea Mobile American Depositary Shares closed at $14.25/$15.00, a 103.5 percent premium to the underlying stock.
"There is no way premiums on KMT will fall below 10 percent," said a trader.
